manifest.name: @local/dsh-advanced-model-editor
manifest.description: Advanced model configuration page for DSH WebUI

scripts.lint: eslint src/ test/ scripts/ && node scripts/build.mjs --check && prettier --check "src/**/*.ts" "test/**/*.mjs" "scripts/*.mjs" "*.mjs" "*.js" "*.json" "*.yml"

bundle.text:
# dsh-advanced-model-editor bundle patch: insert the advanced model settings plugin.
#
# Applied when this bundle appears in a profile's dsh.profile.bundles list.
# The host half (package root) is a no-op plugin node; the browser half
# (dsh.client) is discovered automatically through the package's
# dsh.client declaration + exports["./client"].

- insert:
    - id: model-advanced
      name: '@local/dsh-advanced-model-editor'

readme.text:
A DeepSeek Harness WebUI plugin that adds an **Advanced Model Configuration** section to the
Settings page. It manages LLM provider profiles across the settings namespaces — the
custom provider namespace (`llm-pi-ai`) and the official provider namespace
(`llm-deepseek`) — including built-in and custom providers, model lists,
reasoning/thinking options, headers, retry policy and more, with the same validation
and conflict rules as the official settings UI.

Reads and writes ride DSH's shared settings services (`ctx.configForms` /
`ctx.settingsSchema`), so this page and the official Models page share one document
mirror and one revision queue instead of racing each other. The section appears only
while one of its namespaces is actually served, and it shows the provider facts DSH
directory reports — the endpoint a profile inherits (`defaultBaseURL` / `baseURLEnv`),
the route's own authentication (`nativeAuth`, including OAuth) and any catalog
diagnostic — so a keyless route no longer reads as a missing credential.

The official DeepSeek card also shows how its catalog relates to the service's
model listing: whether the route still follows `GET /models`, whether an edited
catalog replaced it, or whether the endpoint is not the official one at all — with
a **Restore defaults** action that clears the override and resumes the listing.

- **DSH** `>= 0.2.2-rc.1` — only the current release is supported. There is no
  backward-compatibility layer for older DSH versions.
- **Node.js** `^22.19 || >=24`.

---

Install directly from the GitHub `dist` branch (pre-built by CI, no manual clone or compilation required):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:u9521/dsh-advanced-model-editor#dist
```

Then **restart web** (`dsh web`) and **hard-refresh** your browser (Cmd+Shift+R). The plugin appears as **Advanced Model Configuration** in Settings.

Use the `dsh plugin update` command to pull the latest dist release:

```sh

dsh plugin --profile web add github:u9521/dsh-advanced-model-editor#dist
```

Then **restart web** and **hard-refresh** your browser.

---

- **pnpm installed** — `npx get-pnpm` (see https://pnpm.io/installation; alternatives:
  `corepack enable` or `npm install -g pnpm`). Required both for building and because
  `dsh plugin --profile web add` forwards to pnpm internally.
- **Node.js** `^22.19 || >=24`.

Clone the repository into the recommended location:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/u9521/dsh-advanced-model-editor.git ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-advanced-model-editor
cd ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-advanced-model-editor
```

The build output (`lib/`) is not committed to the source branch — build it yourself for local development:

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run build
```

`pnpm run build` runs `tsc` (type check + emit `lib/types/`) and `tsdown` (bundle
`lib/index.js` + `lib/client.js`) with the project's own dependencies — no DSH source
checkout is needed. The browser half is a self-contained closure factory for the DSH
client module table; the whole platform-module contract lives in `tsdown.config.mjs`.

Verify the build with:

```sh
pnpm test
```

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-advanced-model-editor
```

Then **restart web** (`dsh web`) and **hard-refresh** the browser (Cmd+Shift+R).

---

| Command | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `pnpm run build` | Full build (runs `tsc` type check + generates `lib/` bundles) |
| `pnpm run check` | Type check only (`tsc --noEmit`) without emitting files |
| `pnpm test` | Full build, then run the test suite (`node --test`) |
| `pnpm run lint` | ESLint, type check, test suite, and Prettier check in one pass (CI gate) |
| `pnpm run lint:fix` | Apply ESLint fixes, then rewrite the files with Prettier |
| `pnpm run fmt` | Format source and config files with Prettier |
| `pnpm run fmt:check` | Check code formatting compliance |

When installed locally, the plugin is linked via `link:` into the profile. Upgrading local sources only requires **pulling the latest commit and rebuilding** — no need to re-run `dsh plugin add`:

```sh
cd ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-advanced-model-editor
git pull
pnpm run build
```

*(If dependencies changed, run `pnpm install` before building)*

Then **restart web** (`dsh web`) and **hard-refresh** the browser (Cmd+Shift+R).

---

Whether installed from GitHub or linked from local sources, uninstall with:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove @local/dsh-advanced-model-editor
```

Restart web and hard-refresh the browser afterwards. If local sources are no longer needed, you can delete the cloned directory:

```sh
rm -rf ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-advanced-model-editor
```
